title: Ecosystem Prospectus: Model Portfolio & Signal Mapping
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Objective: produce an operational 'prospectus' that ranks and maps emerging and incumbent open models into a prioritized portfolio for Redwood product and GTM consideration. Scope includes taxonomy of signals, a quantitative scoring rubric (performance / cost / license risk / operational fit), an ingestion plan for continuous signals, and a set of recommended short/medium/long-list models for Hosted/Dedicated/Private offerings.

Why: PM leadership needs a decision-ready artifact to guide model onboarding, procurement commitments for Dedicated, and engineering work prioritization for runtime optimizations. The deliverable will be used by Product, Research, Eng, and Sales.

Key tasks: 
- Define signal taxonomy (release cadence, benchmark deltas, license changes, enterprise adoption signals, security advisories).
- Design a 7-factor scoring rubric with weightings and cutoffs (accuracy proxies, latency percentile, per-token cost estimate, quantization friendliness, engineering integration effort, license risk, security maturity).
- Run an initial sweep (10–15 candidates) to populate the portfolio spreadsheet and collect benchmark artifacts.
- Create a watchlist & alerting triggers for high volatility signals (license change, model deprecation, critical CVE, sudden benchmark regressions).
- Deliver a short PRD + recommended model list with rationale for: Hosted tier, Dedicated tier (predictable throughput), and Private deployments (licensed/regulated).

Trade-offs considered so far: favor models with stable CSI (compatibility + infra support) over one-off SOTA wins; weight enterprise license risk higher for Private tier recommendations; accept slightly higher latency at Hosted if cost per token significantly improves margins.

Dependencies: ENG teams for benchmark harness (ENG-3221), Research for eval datasets (ENG-4410 / PM-51720), Legal for license risk review.

Deliverables: prospectus spreadsheet (link), confluence PRD (link), benchmark dashboard (link), watchlist feed (GH webhook + daily ingestion).
acceptance_criteria: Prospectus spreadsheet populated with at least 12 candidate models and scored across the rubric
PRD with recommended lists for Hosted / Dedicated / Private with clear rationale and cost estimates
Benchmarks uploaded to the central dashboard with reproducible run notes and harness commits
Watchlist ingestion pipeline stubbed and producing synthetic signals to verify alert rules
Stakeholder sign-off from Product lead and Head of Research
comments: 2025-11-10 - Kickoff with Research: agreed to prioritize models that have both public evals and reproducible checkpoints. Action: Research to seed 8 initial candidates (Aisha).
2025-12-02 - Engineering review: ENG-3221 will deliver benchmark harness v0 by 2026-01-15. Decision: use 512-token median latency for ops cost estimates. (Reviewer: Jenna Brooks)
2026-01-20 - Legal flagged two models with ambiguous AGPL-derived clauses. Action: put them in 'watch' and request formal legal memo (Legal owner: Priya Gupta).
2026-02-05 - PM review: adjusted rubric weights to increase license risk multiplier for Private recommendations. Rationale: enterprise procurement feedback (sales call with Acme Health).
2026-02-18 - Draft prospectus shared with GTM and Solutions Engineers. Feedback: add explicit migration cost estimates for customers moving from Hosted to Dedicated. Added as sub-task.
2026-02-20 - Status: completed initial scoring for 14 models; next: run reproducible benchmark runs for top 5 and prepare PRD for exec review on 2026-03-03.
notes: Preliminary decision to maintain a three-tier watchlist: Green (safe), Amber (monitor monthly), Red (blocklist/avoid for Private).
We will seed automated signals from: ModelHub release RSS, GitHub release webhooks, PapersWithCode leaderboards, and enterprise procurement requests.

Short-list candidate winners for immediate onboarding experimentation: one high-quality open model, one low-cost quantized candidate, one licensed model for Private trials (names captured in spreadsheet).
Next steps: finalize benchmark runs, complete legal memos for Amber models, prepare executive one-pager and cost delta slides for 2026-03-10 leadership sync.
